title: The Meadow Above the Vech
_design: The case that makes the Kalendar of the Dead decide something, and the only one in the build that produces a DEFECT. Everything the player is trained to check comes back clean: Dietrich's second lion is not the dead first die from Grellwater, it carries DEI GRATIA, was cut in 1207 and is live in 1210; the seventh year of Aldric reduces without argument. The seal is genuine and the date is genuine. What is wrong is on the witness list, and only the Kalendar can say so: Herbord Gantz, castellan of Thurnstadt, is entered in the Margrave's chapel roll as dead in the fifth year of Aldric, two years before this grant. One dead witness is a DEFECT and not a FATAL, because a stale name copied forward from an exemplar is ordinary and two would be a fabrication. So the answer is REFER, and it is the first and only time in the game that REFER means 'this instrument is broken, send it back for correction' rather than 'two laws disagree'. The other witness, Hugo Wend, is given no house at all, so the same packet teaches both halves of the rolls' authority: one name the roll positively condemns, one it cannot speak about and therefore says nothing about.
correct_reason_text: The seal is live and the date reduces cleanly, but Herbord Gantz was two years dead when this was witnessed.

documents.title: Passage docket
documents.claim_summary: Claims the meadow above the Vech by grant of Dietrich, Margrave of Thurn. Produces one sealed charter.
documents.doorkeeper_note: Has waited in more campaigns than passages. Appears to consider both the same thing.

documents.title: Grant of Dietrich, Margrave of Thurn
documents.body_text:
Dietrich, by the grace of God Margrave of Thurn, to all his faithful men, greeting.

For the long service of Gero Kalt in our household we grant him the meadow above the Vech, between the alder bank and the old road, to hold for his life free of every service except the keeping of one horse.

In witness whereof we have set our seal.

seal.note: The second lion, with DEI GRATIA in full.

lines.text: Gero Kalt, of the Margrave's old household. The meadow is not a great matter. That is why I would prefer not to lose a day to it.
The widow's wax bore Dietrich's first words. Mine bears the words he used after 1207. A lion can grow older, whatever her copyist believed.
You admitted the first lion on Tuesday. I have brought you the second. I hope the extra words still matter.
The widow's packet is tied upstairs. Mine need not join it. This die was alive when it touched the wax.
DEI GRATIA. Those are the words he added when the second die was cut. Men change titles more often than lions.
There are the two of them. Mine is the later entry, and the date sits between its cutting and its breaking.
The chapel's roll. Whatever is written in it, I stood at that muster and so did every man on that list. I would put my hand on it.
I said it was a small matter. Small matters have a way of taking exactly as long as large ones in this building.

outcomes.reaction: Good. I had begun to fear a second lion required a second morning.
outcomes.register_note: Confirmed on a live die and a sound date. The witness list was not carried against the rolls.
outcomes.aftermath: The meadow was entered. Four years later the chapel at Thurnstadt was asked for its roll in another matter, and the castellan's obit was read out in open court; the grant was reopened, and the men who had confirmed it were named.

outcomes.reaction: Then write down which part died before Dietrich did. I would like to know what I am meant to mourn.
outcomes.register_note: Refused. The die was live at the date and the grant itself was not impeached.
outcomes.aftermath: Thurn asked on what ground a live seal had been refused. The packet recorded a dead witness and no finding that the grant was false, which are not the same objection.

outcomes.reaction: Upstairs, for a name. He was at the muster that year, I would have sworn it. But I was not the one holding the pen.
outcomes.register_note: Referred for correction. Herbord Gantz, castellan of Thurnstadt, is entered in the Margrave's chapel roll as dead in the fifth year of Aldric; the instrument is dated the seventh. The seal and the date stand.
outcomes.aftermath: The chapel returned a corrected list with two names struck and one added. The meadow was granted again on the amended instrument, to the same man, in the following spring.
